# Level 1 Student Handout: Character, Society & Family
**Age Group:** Ages 6-8 (Level 1 Track: Primary Stage 1)  
**Core Strands:** Excellence to Parents (Birr al-Walidayn) | Spreading Salam | Smiling is Charity | Gentleness to Animals  
**Classical Text Spine:** *Mukhtasar al-Akhdari* (Spiritual Adab) & Nawawi Selections  
**Riwayah & Surah Target:** Hafs 'an 'Asim (Juz' 30: Surah Al-Ma'un & Surah Al-'Asr)

---

## 1. Parents: Our Greatest Blessing
Who stayed awake when you had a high fever? Who packed your lunchbox with loving care? Who works hard every day to provide your warm home and food?

Allah commands in the Holy Quran to treat parents with supreme love and gentleness:  
> **وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا**  
> *"And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and treat your parents with absolute excellence!"* (Surah Al-Isra' 17:23).

### How to Make Mum & Dad Smile Every Day:
1. **Listen the first time:** When Mum asks you to tidy your toys or wash your hands, respond happily with *"Yes, Mum!"* without sighing or saying "Uff!".
2. **Show gratitude:** Walk up to Dad and say: *"I love you, Dad! Thank you for working so hard for our family!"*
3. **Make the Quranic Du'a for them:**  
   > **رَّبِّ ٱرْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِى صَغِيرًا**  
   > *"Rabbir-hamhuma kama rabbayani saghira!"*  
   > (My Lord, have mercy upon my parents, just as they raised me when I was small!).
4. **Safety and honesty:** We obey parents in all good things. But remember: if anyone ever tells you to keep a bad secret or asks you to do something wrong, always tell a trusted adult, because we never obey anyone in disobedience to Allah.

---

## 2. Spreading Salam: The Greeting of Peace
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught us the best words to say when meeting anyone:  
> **أَفْشُوا السَّلاَمَ بَيْنَكُمْ**  
> *"Spread peace (Salam) among yourselves!"* (Sahih Muslim 54).

* When you enter your home, say: **“As-Salamu 'Alaykum!”** (Peace be upon you!). The angels enter with you and bring blessings to your home.
* When someone greets you, reply with even more love: **“Wa 'Alaykum As-Salam wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh!”** (And upon you be peace, the mercy of Allah, and His blessings!).

---

## 3. Smiling is Charity (Sadaqah)
Did you know that you do not need gold coins to give charity? Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was always smiling warmly at children!
* The Prophet ﷺ said: *"Your smile in the face of your brother is charity for you"* (Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1956).
* A cheerful smile brings joy to others.
* When a new classmate looks nervous or shy, give them a warm smile and invite them to play with you.

---

## 4. The Merciful Heart: Kindness to Animals and Nature
Islam is a religion of mercy to every living thing:
* **The Thirsty Dog:** Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told the story of a traveler in the desert who was very thirsty. After drinking from a well, he saw a dog panting and licking moist sand from thirst. The kind traveler climbed down the well, filled his leather shoe with water, carried it up in his teeth, and gave it to the dog. Allah appreciated his mercy and forgave his sins (Sahih al-Bukhari 2363, Sahih Muslim 2244).
* **The Mother Bird:** Once, a companion took two chicks from a nest. The mother bird flew around flapping her wings in grief. The Prophet ﷺ said with compassion: *"Who has hurt this bird by taking her children? Return her chicks to her immediately!"* (Sunan Abi Dawud 2675).
* **Caring for Nature:** Never break branches off trees for fun, never harm tiny creatures, and never let the water tap run wastefully.

# Level 1 Quiz: Character, Society & Family

## Part A: Multiple Choice Questions
1. How should a young Muslim respond when their mother or father calls them?
   (A) Wait until they call three times before answering.
   (B) Complain and ask why someone else cannot go instead.
   (C) Answer immediately and cheerfully with "Yes Mum" or "Yes Dad!"
   (D) Pretend not to hear and keep playing games.

2. What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about smiling at someone?
   (A) It is only required on Eid morning.
   (B) It should only be done for people we already know well.
   (C) It is something only teachers and parents should do.
   (D) It is an act of charity (Sadaqah) that brings joy.

3. How does Islam teach us to treat animals and pets?
   (A) With gentleness, kindness, and providing food and clean water.
   (B) Leaving them alone without water or shelter.
   (C) Only caring for animals that have expensive fur.
   (D) Scaring them when they try to rest in the shade.

4. What special Quranic prayer (du'a) from Surah Al-Isra' do we recite for our parents?
   (A) "My Lord, grant me many toys and candies."
   (B) "My Lord, have mercy upon them, just as they raised me when I was small."
   (C) "My Lord, make every day a holiday."
   (D) "My Lord, forgive only my older relatives."

5. What is the beautiful greeting of peace that Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told us to spread?
   (A) Subhan Allah.
   (B) Astaghfirullah.
   (C) As-Salamu 'Alaykum.
   (D) La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

## Part B: Fill in the Blanks
Vocabulary Bank: Charity, Mercy, Parents
1. Smiling at your brother or sister is an act of ______.
2. We must always be kind, loving, and respectful to our ______.
3. We pray that Allah showers His ______ upon our mothers and fathers.

## Part C: Matching Terms
* Smiling ─── An act of charity (Sadaqah) that brings joy
* Parents ─── Blessed family members we must honor and obey in good
* Gentle Care ─── Treating animals, birds, and nature with compassion

## Part D: Reflection & Application
1. What is one kind action you will do today to make your mother or father smile?
2. Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell the companion to return the baby chicks to their mother bird?

## Answer Key & Marking Guide
1. C - Responding promptly and cheerfully honors parents with excellence (Surah Al-Isra' 17:23).
2. D - The Prophet ﷺ taught that smiling in the face of your brother is charity (Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1956).
3. A - Islam commands kindness and feeding animals, as in the story of the thirsty dog (Sahih al-Bukhari 2363).
4. B - Surah Al-Isra' 17:24 teaches the du'a: "Rabbir-hamhuma kama rabbayani saghira."
5. C - Spreading Salam spreads love and peace among believers (Sahih Muslim 54).

2. Parents - Honorable family members.
3. Mercy - Divine blessing prayed for parents.

* Smiling connects with An act of charity (Sadaqah) that brings joy.
* Parents connects with Blessed family members we must honor and obey in good.
* Gentle Care connects with Treating animals, birds, and nature with compassion.

- Question 1: Awards full points for naming a specific, realistic act of kindness at home (tidying room, saying thank you, listening promptly).
- Question 2: Awards full points for explaining that the Prophet ﷺ felt compassion for the mother bird's sadness and commanded mercy for all living creatures.

# Level 2 Student Handout: Character, Society & Family
**Age Group:** Ages 8-10 (Level 2 Track: Primary Stage 2)  
**Core Strands:** Filial Piety (Birr al-Walidayn) | Family Ties (Silat al-Rahim) | Rights of Neighbors & Teachers | Controlling Anger & Guarding the Tongue  
**Classical Text Spine:** *Matn al-'Ashmawiyyah* & Imam an-Nawawi's *40 Hadith* (Hadiths 13, 15, 16)  
**Riwayah & Surah Target:** Hafs 'an 'Asim (Juz' 30: Surah Al-Humazah & Surah Al-Ma'un)

---

## 1. Birr al-Walidayn: Excellence to Parents
A man came to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and asked: *"O Messenger of Allah! Who among the people is most deserving of my good companionship?"*  
The Prophet ﷺ answered:  
> **أُمُّكَ** (*"Your mother!"*)  
> The man asked: *"Then who?"*  
> The Prophet ﷺ repeated: **أُمُّكَ** (*"Your mother!"*)  
> The man asked a third time: *"Then who?"*  
> The Prophet ﷺ repeated again: **أُمُّكَ** (*"Your mother!"*)  
> The man asked a fourth time: *"Then who?"*  
> The Prophet ﷺ replied: **أَبُوكَ** (*"Then your father!"*)  
> (Sahih al-Bukhari 5971, Sahih Muslim 2548).

The mother carries the child through nine months of pregnancy, endures the pain of childbirth, feeds her baby, and stays awake nights nursing them when sick. Islam gives the mother three times the honor, while also strictly obligating deep respect, support, and obedience to the father.

| Sequence of Honor | Recipient | Significance in Islamic Tradition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **First Mention** | Your Mother | Enduring pregnancy and physical exhaustion |
| **Second Mention** | Your Mother | Enduring the labor and pain of delivery |
| **Third Mention** | Your Mother | Sleepless nights of nursing and early care |
| **Fourth Mention** | Then Your Father | Striving to protect, provide, and guide the family |

### Safeguarding Boundary:
We honor and obey parents in all good deeds. However, the Prophet ﷺ set an absolute boundary: *"There is no obedience to a creature in disobedience to the Creator"* (Sahih Muslim 1840). If anyone ever asks you to commit a sin, harm someone, or keep a harmful secret, you must refuse and immediately inform a trusted teacher or counselor.

---

## 2. Silat al-Rahim: Upholding Family Ties
Allah created families to be tied together by love, mercy, and mutual support:
* **Who are your Rahim?** Grandparents, aunts (*Khala* / *'Ammah*), uncles (*Khal* / *'Amm*), and cousins.
* **The Blessing of Family Ties:** The Prophet ﷺ promised:  
  > *"Whoever loves that their wealth be expanded and their lifespan be prolonged, let them maintain their family ties!"* (Sahih al-Bukhari 2067, Sahih Muslim 2557).
* Even if a relative annoys you, be the bigger person: call them on Eid, exchange gifts, and forgive quickly.

---

## 3. The Rights of Neighbors and Teachers
* **The Neighbor's Sacred Status:** The Prophet ﷺ said:  
  > *"Angel Jibril kept advising me about the rights of the neighbor so intensely that I thought he was about to give neighbors a share of inheritance!"* (Sahih al-Bukhari 6014, Sahih Muslim 2624).  
  * Classical scholars noted that the neighborly circle extends to forty houses in every direction!
  * Never make loud noise late at night that disturbs neighbors.
  * Share warm food and treats when cooking special meals.
  * Help elderly neighbors carry groceries or shovel pathways.
* **Honoring Your Teachers:** Scholars and teachers carry the inheritance of the Prophets. Listen attentively in class, do your schoolwork diligently, never speak rudely, and make du'a for your teachers every single day.

---

## 4. Controlling Anger and Guarding the Tongue
A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: *"Advise me!"* The Prophet ﷺ replied:  
> **لاَ تَغْضَبْ** (*"Do not become angry!"*)  
The man repeated his request several times, and the Prophet ﷺ answered every time: *"Do not become angry!"* (Sahih al-Bukhari 6116).

### The Prophetic Remedy for Anger:
1. **Seek Refuge in Allah:** Say immediately: *“A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim!”*
2. **Remain Silent:** Close your mouth until your anger cools, so you do not say hurtful words.
3. **Change Your Posture:** If you are standing, sit down; if sitting, lie down (Sunan Abi Dawud 4782).
4. **Make Cool Wudu:** Anger is like a fire; cool water extinguishes fire.

### Guarding the Tongue: Two Deadly Sins
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warned against two specific sins of the tongue:
* **Backbiting (*Ghibah*):** Talking about an absent person in a way they would dislike, even if what you say is true! The Prophet ﷺ defined it in Sahih Muslim 2589. If it is false, it is slander (*Buhtan*).
* **Tale-Bearing (*Namimah*):** Carrying gossip between people to cause fights or break up friendships. The Prophet ﷺ warned: *"The tale-bearer will not enter Paradise"* (Sahih al-Bukhari 216, Sahih Muslim 105).

# Level 2 Quiz: Character, Society & Family

## Part A: Multiple Choice Questions
1. How many times did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ repeat "Your mother" when asked who is most deserving of good companionship?
   (A) One time.
   (B) Two times.
   (C) Five times.
   (D) Three times.

2. What does the term Birr al-Walidayn mean in Islamic ethics?
   (A) Deep excellence, devotion, and loving honor shown to parents.
   (B) Asking parents for financial allowance each week.
   (C) Keeping family history records in a book.
   (D) Moving far away to live independently without communication.

3. What golden counsel did the Prophet ﷺ repeatedly give to the man who asked him for advice?
   (A) "Fast every single day without interruption."
   (B) "Do not become angry" (La Taghdab).
   (C) "Travel to every country in the world."
   (D) "Remain awake all night every night."

4. How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ define Ghibah (backbiting) in Sahih Muslim?
   (A) Greeting someone with words of peace in their presence.
   (B) Reminding a friend to perform the noon prayer on time.
   (C) Speaking about an absent person in a way they would dislike, even if it is true.
   (D) Offering constructive advice to a classmate in private.

5. What dual blessings did the Prophet ﷺ promise for those who faithfully maintain family kinship ties (Silat al-Rahim)?
   (A) Gaining high scores on school examinations without studying.
   (B) Never experiencing any sickness or difficulty in life.
   (C) Becoming a political ruler of an empire.
   (D) Expansion and blessing in provision, and a lengthened, blessed lifespan.

## Part B: Fill in the Blanks
Vocabulary Bank: Ghibah, Mother, Three, Silat al-Rahim
1. The Prophet ﷺ emphasized honoring the ______ three times before mentioning the father.
2. Maintaining loving and supportive bonds with relatives is called ______.
3. The Prophet ﷺ repeated his counsel against anger ______ times.
4. Mentioning an absent person with what they dislike is known as ______.

## Part C: Matching Terms
* Birr al-Walidayn ─── Supreme excellence and devotion to parents
* Silat al-Rahim ─── Upholding loving ties of kinship with relatives
* La Taghdab ─── Prophetic counsel: "Do not become angry"
* Ghibah ─── Speaking about an absent person in a manner they dislike

## Part D: Reflection & Application
1. Think of a situation where someone feels angry. What are two Sunnah steps they can take immediately to calm down?
2. Why is carrying gossip between people (Namimah) considered so destructive to friendships and community trust?

## Answer Key & Marking Guide
1. D - The Prophet ﷺ repeated "Your mother" three times before saying "Then your father" (Sahih al-Bukhari 5971, Sahih Muslim 2548).
2. A - Birr al-Walidayn is the Quranic obligation of showing supreme excellence and kindness to parents (Surah Al-Isra' 17:23).
3. B - In Sahih al-Bukhari 6116, the Prophet ﷺ repeated three times: "Do not become angry."
4. C - In Sahih Muslim 2589, the Prophet ﷺ defined backbiting as mentioning your brother with what he dislikes.
5. D - Sahih al-Bukhari 2067 and Sahih Muslim 2557 state that maintaining ties of kinship expands provision and prolongs life.

### Fill in the Blanks Key
1. Mother - Honored three times.
2. Silat al-Rahim - Kinship bonds.
3. Three - Repeated counsel.
4. Ghibah - Backbiting.

### Matching Key
* Birr al-Walidayn connects with Supreme excellence and devotion to parents.
* Silat al-Rahim connects with Upholding loving ties of kinship with relatives.
* La Taghdab connects with Prophetic counsel: "Do not become angry".
* Ghibah connects with Speaking about an absent person in a manner they dislike.

### Reflection Marking Rubric
- Question 1: Awards full points for identifying two Prophetic remedies: seeking refuge from Shaytan, remaining silent, sitting/lying down, or making wudu.
- Question 2: Awards full points for explaining that Namimah destroys trust, breeds suspicion, causes hostility, and carries the warning that the tale-bearer will not enter Paradise.

# Level 3 Student Handout: Character, Society & Family
**Age Group:** Ages 10-12 (Level 3 Track: Years 5 & 6)  
**Topics:** Sincerity (Ikhlas) vs. Ostentation (Riya'), Guarding the Tongue (Ghibah & Namimah), Filial Piety (Birr al-Walidayn), and The Rights of Neighbors  
**Classical Text Spine:** *Al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyyah* (Hadiths 11 to 20) & *Al-Adab al-Mufrad* of Imam al-Bukhari  
**Riwayah & Tajweed:** Hafs 'an 'Asim (Juz' 30: Surah Al-A'la and Al-Layl)

---

## 1. The Heart of Faith: Sincerity (*Ikhlas*)

Welcome to Level 3 Character and Ethics! In Islam, outward good deeds carry no spiritual weight if the inner intention is corrupt. The foundational Hadith of the entire religion states:  
*“Actions are judged only by intentions, and every person will have only what they intended.”* (Sahih al-Bukhari 1, Sahih Muslim 1907).

| Spiritual Dimension | Al-Ikhlas (Sincerity) | Al-Riya' (Ostentation / Showing Off) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Definition** | Performing good deeds solely for the pleasure of Allah. | Performing good deeds to impress people or win praise. |
| **Motive** | Seeking divine reward and pleasing the Creator. | Craving social approval, attention, or internet likes. |
| **Spiritual Status** | The foundation of all accepted worship. | Classified as the "Hidden Shirk" (*Al-Shirk al-Khafi*). |
| **Outcome** | Enduring reward and spiritual peace in Paradise. | The deed is rejected and earns spiritual punishment. |

---

## 2. Guarding the Tongue: Three Destructive Sins of Speech

The Prophet ﷺ said:  
*“Whoever can guarantee for me what is between his two jawbones (the tongue) and what is between his two legs, I guarantee for him Paradise!”* (Sahih al-Bukhari 6474).

At ages 10-12, schoolyard banter and group messaging can easily slip into three poisonous sins of the tongue:

1. **Al-Ghibah (الْغِيبَة), Backbiting:**  
   The Prophet ﷺ defined it: *"Mentioning your brother in a way he would dislike."* Someone asked: *"What if what I said is true about him?"* The Prophet ﷺ replied: *"If it is true, you have backbitten him; and if it is false, you have slandered him (*Bahattahu*)!"* (Sahih Muslim 2589).  
   *The Quranic Warning:* Surah Al-Hujurat (49:12) compares backbiting to eating the dead flesh of your own brother.
2. **Al-Namimah (النَّمِيمَة), Tale-Bearing:**  
   Carrying words between friends to cause hostility and broken friendships. The Prophet ﷺ warned: *"The tale-bearer will not enter Paradise!"* (Sahih al-Bukhari 216, Sahih Muslim 105).
3. **Al-Buhtan (الْبُهْتَان), Slander and False Accusation:**  
   Inventing false claims about an innocent person to harm their reputation.

---

## 3. Filial Piety: *Birr al-Walidayn* (Honoring Parents)

Allah pairs worship of Him with supreme excellence to parents:  
*“And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to parents. Whether one or both of them reach old age with you, say not to them a word of disrespect (not even 'Uff!'), nor shout at them, but address them with noble speech.”* (Surah Al-Isra' 17:23).

### Practical Ways to Practice *Birr* Every Day:
1. **Never say "Uff!":** Avoid rolling eyes, sighing in frustration, or slamming doors when asked to clean up or study.
2. **Listen Attentively:** When your mother or father speaks, put down devices and make respectful eye contact.
3. **Make the Quranic Du'a Daily:**  
   `رَّبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا`  
   *“My Lord, have mercy upon them both as they brought me up when I was small!”* (Surah Al-Isra' 17:24).
4. **The Sacred Safeguard:** While honoring parents is a supreme duty, obedience is bounded by goodness. The Prophet ﷺ stated: *“There is no obedience to anyone in disobedience to Allah”* (Sahih al-Bukhari 7257, Sahih Muslim 1840). If anyone pressures you to harm someone, lie, or keep unsafe secrets, you must refuse and inform a trusted teacher or counselor.

---

## 4. The Sacred Rights of Neighbors and Fellow Muslims

The Prophet ﷺ said:  
*“Jibril kept advising me about good treatment of the neighbor until I thought he would make him an heir!”* (Sahih al-Bukhari 6014, Sahih Muslim 2624).

* **Who is a Neighbor?** Classical Islamic scholars defined the neighborhood as extending **forty houses in every direction**.
* **Universal Kindness:** Whether your neighbor is a Muslim or of another faith, you must protect their peace, share food, avoid loud noise late at night, and assist them during illness or emergencies.
* **The Six Rights of a Muslim:** The Prophet ﷺ taught: *"The rights of a Muslim upon another Muslim are six: When you meet him, greet him with Salam; when he invites you, accept his invitation; when he seeks your advice, advise him sincerely; when he sneezes and praises Allah, reply 'Yarhamukallah'; when he is ill, visit him; and when he passes away, attend his funeral"* (Sahih Muslim 2162).

   (D) To build high walls between adjacent properties to avoid interaction.

# Level 4 Student Handout: Character, Society & Family
**Age Group:** Ages 12-14 (Level 4 Track: Adolescent & Puberty / Years 7 & 8)  
**Topics:** Islamic Brotherhood (Ukhuwwah), Overcoming Anger, Enjoining Good & Social Justice, and The Adab of Knowledge  
**Classical Text Spine:** *Al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyyah* (Hadiths 21 to 35) & *Riyad al-Salihin*  
**Riwayah & Tajweed:** Hafs 'an 'Asim (Juz' 29: Surah Al-Qalam and Al-Haqqah)

---

## 1. Spiritual Brotherhood: *Al-Ukhuwwah al-Islamiyyah*

As you navigate early adolescence, social cliques, peer pressure, and tribal loyalties often dominate school life. Islam shatters superficial cliques by establishing **Ukhuwwah** (spiritual brotherhood and sisterhood) rooted purely in love for Allah.

The Prophet ﷺ said in Hadith 13 of Imam an-Nawawi:  
*“None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself!”* (Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45).

### The Six Rights of a Fellow Muslim (Sahih Muslim 2162):

| Right | Occasion | Practical Etiquette |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Greeting (*Salam*)** | When meeting | Initiate Salam with a warm smile and clear voice. |
| **2. Invitation (*Ijabah*)** | When invited | Attend celebratory or community meals to build love. |
| **3. Sincere Advice (*Nasihah*)** | When consulted | Offer honest, constructive, and compassionate counsel in private. |
| **4. Tashmit** | When sneezing | Say *"Yarhamukallah"* when they sneeze and say *"Alhamdulillah"*. |
| **5. Visiting the Sick** | During illness | Visit, comfort them, make du'a for healing, and offer practical help. |
| **6. Funeral (*Jana'iz*)** | At passing | Attend the funeral prayer and burial to honor their soul. |

* **The Three-Day Limit on Boycotts:** The Prophet ﷺ strictly forbade Muslims from boycotting or refusing to speak to a brother for **more than three days** (Sahih al-Bukhari 6077, Sahih Muslim 2560). The superior of the two is the one who initiates the greeting of Salam first!

---

## 2. Emotional Mastery: The Prophetic Cure for Anger

A man once came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked: *"Advise me!"* The Prophet ﷺ repeated three times:  
**“Do not become angry!” (*La Taghdab*)** (Sahih al-Bukhari 6116).

Islam does not demand that you never feel irritation; rather, it commands you to **master your emotional reactions** rather than becoming a slave to blind rage:
* The Prophet ﷺ asked: *"Who do you consider the strong wrestler among you?"* The companions replied: *"The one who cannot be thrown to the ground by men!"* The Prophet ﷺ corrected them:  
  *“The strong person is not the wrestler; rather, the truly strong person is the one who controls his own soul during anger!”* (Sahih al-Bukhari 6114, Sahih Muslim 2609).

### The Prophetic Step-by-Step Protocol for Anger:
1. **Seek Refuge:** Say immediately: *A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim*.
2. **Change Physical Posture:** If you are standing, sit down; if you are sitting, lie down (Sunan Abi Dawud 4782). Lowering your physical posture cools adrenaline.
3. **Perform Wudu:** Water extinguishes the heat of demonic rage.
4. **Remain Silent:** Never send an angry text message, post a comment, or speak in rage. Wait until the storm clears.

---

## 3. Social Justice and Enjoining Good: Hadith 34

The Prophet ﷺ commanded:  
*“Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.”* (Sahih Muslim 49).

| Tier of Intervention | Level of Authority | Practical Application |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. By the Hand (*Bil-Yad*)** | Legitimate lawful jurisdiction | Parents in the home, teachers in the classroom, or lawful civic authorities in society. Unlawful vigilantism is strictly forbidden. |
| **2. By the Tongue (*Bil-Lisan*)** | Spoken and written advocacy | Speaking up for a bullied classmate, explaining truth respectfully, offering gentle private advice (*Nasihah*), or reporting abuse. |
| **3. By the Heart (*Bil-Qalb*)** | Inner spiritual rejection | When physical intervention and speech would cause greater harm, detesting the wrong in the heart and refusing to participate. |

### The Sacred Safeguarding Standard:
Legitimate authority is bounded by divine law. The Prophet ﷺ declared: *“There is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator”* (Sahih Muslim 1840). If anyone in authority orders something harmful, illegal, or abusive, one must not comply, and should immediately seek help from trusted counselors or child protection advocates.

---

## 4. The Sacred Adab of Seeking Knowledge (*Adab Talab al-'Ilm*)

When Imam Malik was a boy, his mother dressed him in scholarly clothes and advised him:  
*“Go to Rabi'ah and learn from his Adab (manners and reverence) before you learn his knowledge!”* (Reported by Qadi 'Iyad in *Tartib al-Madarik*).

In his classical manual *Tadhkirat al-Sami'*, Qadi Ibn Jama'ah outlines essential student etiquette:
* **Humility Before the Teacher:** Listen attentively even if you have heard the lesson before. Never speak over your instructor.
* **Preparedness:** Bring your notebook, pen, and texts ready; sit with upright, alert posture.
* **The Sincerity of Inquiry:** Ask questions to understand and practice, never to show off intelligence or humiliate a classmate.

# Level 4 Quiz: Character, Society & Family

## Part A: Multiple Choice Questions
1. How does Prophet Muhammad ﷺ define the standard of complete faith in Hadith 13 of Imam an-Nawawi?
   (A) By memorizing historical genealogies without error.
   (B) Loving for your brother what you love for yourself.
   (C) Accumulating significant financial wealth for travel.
   (D) Constructing large public buildings with tall arches.

2. What is the maximum time limit allowed for two Muslims to boycott or refuse to speak to one another following a dispute?
   (A) Three days.
   (B) Twenty-four hours only.
   (C) One full lunar year.
   (D) Indefinitely until an elder commands reconciliation.

3. According to authentic prophetic tradition, who is the superior party when two Muslims reconcile after a disagreement?
   (A) The one who remains completely silent until approached.
   (B) The one who hires a mediator to deliver a written apology.
   (C) The one who initiates the greeting of Salam first.
   (D) The one who pays a financial settlement to the other party.

4. What golden counsel did the Prophet ﷺ repeat three times to the man who asked for life guidance in Hadith 16 of Nawawi?
   (A) "Travel across foreign seas every summer!"
   (B) "Fast continuously without breaking your fast!"
   (C) "Abandon physical work and live in isolation!"
   (D) "Do not become angry!" (La Taghdab).

5. How did the Prophet ﷺ redefine "the truly strong person" (Al-Shadid) in Sahih al-Bukhari?
   (A) The warrior who can defeat twenty opponents in physical combat.
   (B) The one who controls his own soul and temper during moments of anger.
   (C) The merchant who commands the largest caravan in Arabia.
   (D) The runner who finishes first in endurance races.

6. What sequence of physical actions is recommended in the Sunnah when experiencing intense anger?
   (A) Pacing back and forth rapidly while breathing deeply.
   (B) Leaving the house immediately and running around the neighborhood.
   (C) Seeking refuge with Allah, sitting down if standing (or lying down), and making cool wudu.
   (D) Clenching fists and shouting into an empty room.

7. In Hadith 34 of Imam an-Nawawi, what are the three graduated tiers of changing an observed wrong or injustice?
   (A) By the hand (lawful authority), by the tongue (truth and counsel), and by the heart (inner rejection).
   (B) By public shaming, by legal lawsuits, and by economic embargoes.
   (C) By voting, by peaceful rallies, and by private boycotts.
   (D) By financial fines, by exile, and by silent disregard.

8. When is changing a wrong "with the hand" (physical intervention) legally permitted in Islamic jurisprudence?
   (A) By any passerby on the street who disagrees with someone's clothing.
   (B) Only during daylight hours on official holidays.
   (C) By anonymous youth groups enforcing social rules online.
   (D) Exclusively by those holding legitimate legal or custodial jurisdiction (such as parents at home or lawful civic authorities).

9. What advice did Imam Malik's mother give him when he began his pursuit of sacred knowledge?
   (A) "Study mathematics and commerce before touching religious books."
   (B) "Go to Rabi'ah and learn from his Adab (manners and reverence) before his knowledge!"
   (C) "Debate with scholars publicly so people recognize your intelligence."
   (D) "Never write down notes until you have memorized the entire text."

10. What is the correct student etiquette (Adab al-Talib) if a teacher explains a concept you have already studied?
    (A) Listen attentively with humility and reverence, recognizing that reviewing knowledge is a spiritual blessing.
    (B) Interrupt the teacher immediately and announce that you already understand the lesson.
    (C) Look at your mobile phone and whisper to a classmate while waiting for the next topic.
    (D) Stand up and leave the lecture hall to find advanced reading material.

## Part B: Fill in the Blanks
Vocabulary Bank: Three days, Adab, La Taghdab, Hadith 13, Al-Shadid
1. The Prophetic advice repeated three times regarding emotional self-control is ______.
2. Boycotting a fellow Muslim following a dispute is forbidden beyond ______.
3. Loving for your brother what you love for yourself is the core message of Nawawi's ______.
4. The truly strong person who controls his soul during anger is titled ______.
5. Imam Malik taught that a seeker of knowledge must master ______ before learning facts.

## Part C: Matching Terms
* La Taghdab ─── The repeated prophetic counsel to master emotional anger
* Al-Shadid ─── The truly strong person who restrains his temper when provoked
* Ukhuwwah ─── Spiritual brotherhood and sisterhood rooted in love for Allah
* Hadith 34 ─── Changing injustice through hand, tongue, or heart
* Adab al-Talib ─── The sacred etiquette and humility of the student before teachers

## Part D: Reflection & Application
1. A classmate at school insults you in front of other students, tempting you to react with a physical fight or screaming insults. Walk through how you apply the prophetic anger protocol in that exact moment.
2. Analyze the three tiers of Hadith 34: Why did the Prophet ﷺ designate changing evil "in the heart" as the minimum standard of faith?
3. What is the danger of pursuing academic or Islamic knowledge without first mastering personal Adab (manners and humility)?
4. Explain how the Prophetic principle of loving for your brother what you love for yourself transforms peer competition into mutual cooperation.

## Answer Key & Marking Guide
1. B - Hadith 13 establishes empathy and selflessness as the benchmark of mature faith (Sahih al-Bukhari 13, Sahih Muslim 45).
2. A - Transgressing the three-day limit on anger boycotts is strictly forbidden in prophetic Hadith (Sahih al-Bukhari 6077).
3. C - The one who initiates the greeting of Salam breaks pride and earns greater reward.
4. D - The Prophet ﷺ repeated "La Taghdab" to emphasize emotional discipline as life's anchor (Sahih al-Bukhari 6116).
5. B - Spiritual emotional self-control requires far greater strength than mere physical wrestling (Sahih al-Bukhari 6114).
6. C - Seeking refuge, lowering physical posture, and cooling anger with wudu are proven Sunnah methods (Sunan Abi Dawud 4782).
7. A - Changing by hand, tongue, and heart represents the comprehensive framework of enjoining good (Sahih Muslim 49).
8. D - Direct physical intervention requires lawful authority to prevent chaotic vigilantism.
9. B - Imam Malik's mother insisted that character and reverence must precede theoretical learning (Tartib al-Madarik).
10. A - Classical Adab requires sitting with the attentiveness of someone hearing the lesson for the first time.

### Fill in the Blanks Key
1. La Taghdab - Do not become angry.
2. Three days - Anger limit.
3. Hadith 13 - Loving for your brother.
4. Al-Shadid - Truly strong person.
5. Adab - Reverence and manners.

### Matching Key
* La Taghdab connects with The repeated prophetic counsel to master emotional anger.
* Al-Shadid connects with The truly strong person who restrains his temper when provoked.
* Ukhuwwah connects with Spiritual brotherhood and sisterhood rooted in love for Allah.
* Hadith 34 connects with Changing injustice through hand, tongue, or heart.
* Adab al-Talib connects with The sacred etiquette and humility of the student before teachers.

### Reflection Marking Rubric
- Question 1: Awards full points for applying the Sunnah protocol: pausing, seeking refuge with Allah, sitting down, performing wudu, and refusing to respond with retaliatory abuse.
- Question 2: Awards full points for explaining that heart rejection keeps moral clarity alive when outward intervention is physically dangerous or impossible, whereas apathy indicates dead faith.
- Question 3: Awards full points for explaining that knowledge without Adab breeds arrogance, pride, intellectual bullying, and turns religion into a tool for self-promotion.
- Question 4: Awards full points for explaining that genuine love for others eliminates jealousy (Hasad), fosters generous sharing of notes and help, and celebrates peers' achievements.

# Level 5 Senior Seminar Guide: Character, Society & Family
**Age Group:** Ages 14-16+ (Senior High / Level 5 Capstone Track)  
**Topics:** Tazkiyat al-Nafs (Spiritual Purification), Curing the Four Major Heart Diseases (Hasad, Kibr, 'Ujb, Riya'), Junaydi Sufism, and The Architecture of Sincere Repentance  
**Classical Text Spine:** *Matn Ibn 'Ashir* (Tazkiyah Chapter), *Qawa'id al-Tasawwuf* of Sidi Ahmad Zarruq, and *Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din* of Imam al-Ghazali  
**Riwayah & Advanced Tajweed:** Hafs 'an 'Asim with Warsh 'an Nafi' awareness; Tafsir of Surah Al-Hujurat (Ethics of Global Brotherhood)

---

## 1. Tazkiyat al-Nafs: The Science of Heart Purification

In the tripartite definition of the religion revealed in the Hadith of Jibril (Sahih Muslim 8), Islam comprises:
1. **Islam (Shari'ah / Fiqh):** Outward physical submission, ritual observance, and lawful conduct.
2. **Iman ('Aqidah):** Intellectual and rational conviction in Tawhid and the articles of faith.
3. **Ihsan (Tazkiyah / Tasawwuf):** Spiritual purification, worshipping Allah as though you see Him.

Imam 'Abd al-Wahid Ibn 'Ashir concludes his foundational didactic text *Al-Murshid al-Mu'in* with a vital chapter on **Tazkiyah**, defining it according to the orthodox, Shari'ah-bound framework of **Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Junayd al-Baghdadi** (d. 297 AH) and the North African Maliki scholar **Sidi Ahmad Zarruq** (d. 899 AH). In Sunni orthodoxy, true Sufism is not mysticism separated from the law; it is the inward perfection of the Shari'ah.

### The Four Deadly Diseases of the Heart (*Amrad al-Qulub*):

| Spiritual Disease | Arabic Term | Core Psychological Symptom | Inward Malady |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Destructive Envy** | *Al-Hasad* | Resenting blessings given to others and desiring their loss. | Subtle objection to Allah's divine decree (*Qada'*). |
| **2. Arrogance** | *Al-Kibr* | Rejecting truth when challenged and belittling people. | Usurping divine majesty (*Al-Mutakabbir*). |
| **3. Self-Righteous Vanity** | *Al-'Ujb* | Marveling at one's own piety and claiming credit for deeds. | Forgetting Allah's enabling grace (*Tawfiq*). |
| **4. Ostentation** | *Al-Riya'* | Performing acts of worship to gain human praise and status. | Hidden idolatry (*Al-Shirk al-Khafi*). |

---

## 2. Diagnosis and Prescriptions for the Four Heart Diseases

### A. Al-Hasad (Destructive Envy):
* **Diagnosis:** Wishing that a blessing (*Ni'mah*) possessed by another person (intellect, beauty, wealth, popularity) be stripped away from them.
* **Theological Root:** The envier is subtly objecting to **Allah's wisdom and divine decree (*Qada'*)** in distributing gifts!
* **The Spiritual Cure:** Recognize that your envy harms only your own soul while increasing the other's reward. Force yourself to make secret sincere du'a for that person's success and give them gifts.

### B. Al-Kibr (Arrogance):
* **Diagnosis:** The Prophet ﷺ defined it: *"Arrogance is rejecting the truth (*Batar al-Haqq*) and looking down upon people (*Ghamt al-Nas*)!"* (Sahih Muslim 91).
* **The Spiritual Cure:** Meditate on your biological origin: Created from a humble drop of fluid, carrying impurities inside your body every day, and ending as dust beneath the earth. True greatness belongs solely to **Al-Mutakabbir (Allah)**.

### C. Al-'Ujb (Self-Righteous Vanity):
* **Diagnosis:** Becoming infatuated with your own piety, prayers, or good deeds, feeling that you have earned salvation by your personal brilliance.
* **The Spiritual Cure:** Recognize the principle of **Tawfiq (Enabling Grace)**: You only prayed because Allah gave you breath, health, guidance, and permission. If Allah withdrew His enabling grace for one second, you would collapse! Every good deed is purely a divine gift.

### D. Al-Riya' (Ostentation / Seeking Praise):
* **Diagnosis:** Performing worship to be seen, praised, or admired by human beings.
* **The Spiritual Cure:** Train the soul in **secret worship (*'Amal al-Sirr*)**: Give charity where your left hand does not know what your right hand spent (Sahih al-Bukhari 1423, Sahih Muslim 1031); pray tahajjud in dark isolation; meditate on the reality that human praise cannot save you on the Day of Judgment.

---

## 3. The Architecture of Sincere Repentance (*Al-Tawbah al-Nasuhah*)

Imam Ibn 'Ashir outlines the four strict conditions required for repentance to be accepted by Allah:

| Pillar of Tawbah | Meaning | Practical Implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Al-Iqla' (الإقلاع)** | Immediate Desistance | Ceasing the sin immediately without procrastination. |
| **2. Al-Nadam (الندم)** | Genuine Remorse | Feeling deep brokenness before Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said: *"Remorse is repentance"* (Sunan Ibn Majah 4252). |
| **3. Al-'Azm (العزم)** | Firm Determination | Making a sincere, unshakeable covenant never to return to the sin. |
| **4. Radd al-Mazalim (رد المظالم)** | Restoring Rights | If human rights were violated (theft, slander, physical harm), returning stolen assets or seeking direct forgiveness. |

---

## 4. Ash'ari Moral Epistemology & Personal Integrity (*Muru'ah*)

### Revelation as the Criterion of Morals:
In Ash'ari epistemology, moral obligation (*Al-Wujub*) is established through divine revelation (*Al-Shar'*), not merely through human subjective intuition (*Al-'Aql*). While human intellect perceives utility and beauty, only Allah defines what is definitively good (*Husn*) and evil (*Qubh*). This protects believers from secular moral relativism.

### The Standard of 'Adalah and Muru'ah:
In Maliki jurisprudence, a person's testimony and legal reliability depend on:
* **'Adalah:** Moral uprightness, avoiding major sins (*Kaba'ir*), and not persisting in minor sins.
* **Muru'ah:** Personal dignity, chivalry, and good taste that protect one from shameful, undignified behavior in public.

### The Golden Chain of Western Sunni Scholarship:
* **Imam Malik ibn Anas** (d. 179 AH, Madinah): Founder of the legal school.
* **Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani** (d. 386 AH, Kairouan, Tunisia): "Young Malik", author of *Al-Risalah*.
* **Al-Qadi 'Iyad** (d. 544 AH, Ceuta and Granada): Master of Hadith and author of *Al-Shifa*.
* **Imam Shihab al-Din al-Qarafi** (d. 684 AH, Egypt): Master of legal maxims (*Al-Qawa'id*).
* **Imam 'Abd al-Wahid Ibn 'Ashir** (d. 1040 AH, Fes, Morocco): Codifier of Creed, Fiqh, and Tazkiyah.
* **Sidi Ahmad Zarruq** (d. 899 AH, Fes and Tripoli): Great reformer who harmonized Sufi spirituality with orthodox Maliki law in *Qawa'id al-Tasawwuf*.

   (B) Seeking advanced degrees in secular universities.
   (C) Rejecting the truth (Batar al-Haqq) and looking down upon people (Ghamt al-Nas).
   (D) Refusing to eat sweet foods during the week.

   (A) It wastes bodily calories and weakens eyesight.
   (B) It subtly objects to Allah's divine wisdom and decree (Qada') in distributing blessings to His servants.
   (C) It violates the dietary laws of lawful slaughter.
   (D) It prevents a student from memorizing poetry.

4. How does "Al-'Ujb" (Self-Righteous Vanity) differ from "Al-Riya'" (Ostentation) in Islamic spiritual diagnosis?
   (A) Riya' requires human spectators to show off, whereas 'Ujb is internal conceit where a person marvels at their own piety in solitude.
   (B) 'Ujb is looking down on parents, while Riya' is looking down on neighbors.
   (C) 'Ujb applies exclusively to physical wealth, while Riya' applies only to fasting.
   (D) There is no difference; classical scholars treat them as identical terms.

   (A) Meditating on personal achievements and awards.
   (B) Attributing all success to natural genetic advantages.

   (D) Recognizing the concept of Tawfiq (Enabling Divine Grace): that every righteous act is purely a gift from Allah.

# Presentation Slides: Character, Society & Family (Akhlaq & Mu'amalat)
## A Guide for Teachers

---

## Slide 1: Welcome & Course Overview
### Character, Society & Family: The Outer Mirror of the Inner Soul
*   **Subject:** Islamic Studies (Akhlaq & Mu'amalat)
*   **Fiqh School:** Maliki (*Madhhab*)
*   **Creed School:** Ash'ari
*   **Core Focus:** Cultivating beautiful character (*Akhlaq*) internally and expressing it through just, legally sound interactions (*Mu'amalat*) with family, friends, and society.
*   **Key Themes:**
    *   Honesty, Humility, and Anger Management (*Sidq*, *Tawadu'*, *Kadhm al-Ghaydh*)
    *   Rights of Parents, Family, and Neighbors (*Birr al-Walidayn*, *Silat al-Rahim*, *Huquq al-Jiwar*)
    *   Choosing Friends and Navigating Peer Pressure (*Suhbah Salihah*)
    *   Social Media Ethics: Protecting Deen, Mind, and Honor
    *   Justice, Public Interest, and Legal Chivalry (*'Adl*, *Maslahah*, *Muru'ah*)

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Welcome & Objective:** Welcome the students. Explain that this unit transitions from individual worship (*Taharah* and *Salah*) to social responsibility (*Mu'amalat*) and character development (*Akhlaq*).
*   **Pedagogical Note:** Highlight that we are studying these topics through the systematic framework of the **Maliki school of law** and the **Ash'ari school of creed**. Explain that character in Islam is not just an optional set of nice behaviors; it is deeply connected to theological truths and legal obligations.
*   **Discussion Starter:** Ask: *"Can a person have a perfect prayer (Salah) if they go home and treat their parents or neighbors poorly? Why is there a connection between worship and character?"*

---

## Slide 2: Creed Foundation: What Makes an Action "Good"?
### Divine Command Ethics (Al-Husn wal-Qubh al-Shar'iyyan)
*   **How do we know what is moral?**
    *   **Ash'ari Creed Ruling:** Moral goodness (*Al-Husn* / الْحُسْن) and moral badness (*Al-Qubh* / الْقُبْح) are determined directly by Allah's revelation (*Al-Shar'* / الشَّرْع).
*   **The Role of Reason (*'Aql*):**
    *   Human intellect can recognize that truth is useful or pain is bad.
    *   However, intellect alone *cannot* dictate what makes an action rewardable or punishable by Allah.
*   **Worship as Submission:**
    *   We tell the truth, honor parents, and act justly because **Allah commanded us to do so**. 
    *   Morality is not a human social contract; it is a response to Divine Command.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Ash'ari Theology Integration:** This slide introduces a core Ash'ari creed concept: *Al-Husn wal-Qubh al-Shar'iyyan* (Goodness and badness are defined by revelation). Contrast this briefly with the Mu'tazilite view (which held that reason alone can determine what is objectively good or bad in a way that binds Allah's judgment).
*   **Explanation:** Explain that for Ash'aris, if Allah commands something, it is good *because* He commanded it. If He forbids something, it is bad *because* He forbade it. 
*   **Example:** Helping the poor is good because Allah praised it and commanded it. If we only did it because it "felt nice," our reward would be worldly. When we do it because Allah commanded it, it becomes an act of worship (*'ibadah*).

---

## Slide 3: Perfecting Character: The Prophet’s Mission & Human Choice
### Understanding Character (Akhlaq) and Human Action (Kasb)
*   **The Prophetic Statement:** 
    *   The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: *"I was sent only to perfect noble character"* (*Innama bu'ithtu li-utammima makarim al-akhlaq*).
*   **Creed Connection: Acquisition (*Kasb* / كَسْب):**
    *   Allah is the Creator (*Khaliq*) of all actions, both good and bad.
    *   Human beings are the acquirers (*Muktasib*) of their actions.
    *   We use our free will to **choose** to act with honesty or anger, and Allah creates the physical action.
*   **Responsibility:**
    *   Because we choose to acquire the character traits, we are fully accountable (*Mukallaf*) before Allah for our choices.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Ash'ari Concept of Kasb:** Explain *Kasb* (acquisition) simply: Allah alone creates the ability and the action, but He gives humans the choice to direct their intention (*Niyyah*). When we choose to be patient, Allah creates the patience in us. Therefore, we cannot blame our bad temper on "how Allah made us"; we must choose to acquire good character.
*   **Hadith Citation:** The quote is recorded by Imam Malik in the *Muwatta* (Book of Good Character).
*   **Pedagogical Tip:** Emphasize that *Akhlaq* (plural of *Khuluq*) is not just passive personality; it is active choice and training of the soul (*Riyadat al-Nafs*).

---

## Slide 4: Honesty (Sidq): The Root of Trust
### Truthfulness in Word, Deed, and State
*   **What is Sidq?**
    *   **Sidq** (صِدْق) means truthfulness, sincerity, and consistency.
*   **Three Levels of Honesty:**
    1.  **Truth in Speech (*Sidq al-Lisan*):** Never telling lies, even in jest.
    2.  **Truth in Action (*Sidq al-'Amal*):** Making sure your outer actions match your inner intentions. No hypocrisy (*Nifaq*).
    3.  **Truth in Intention (*Sidq al-Niyyah*):** Doing good purely for the sake of Allah, not to show off (*Riya'*).
*   **The Ultimate Status:**
    *   The Prophet (pbuh) said: *"Truthfulness leads to righteousness (*Birr*), and righteousness leads to Paradise."* (Agreed upon).

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Concept Breakdown:** Discuss how honesty goes beyond just "not telling lies." It means being authentic.
*   **Fiqh Literacy Link:** In Islamic law, a single lie can destroy a person's legal credibility. In the Maliki school, a person who is caught lying is classified as having compromised integrity (*Fasiq*) and their testimony in court is rejected.
*   **Interactive Discussion:** *"Is it ever okay to lie to make people laugh?"* Explain that the Prophet (pbuh) warned against lying even when joking: *"Woe to the one who speaks and lies to make the people laugh..."* (Abu Dawud).

---

## Slide 5: Humility (Tawadu'): Defeating the Ego
### Overcoming Pride (Kibr) in the Heart
*   **What is Tawadu'?**
    *   **Tawadu'** (تَوَاضُع) is humility, the state of recognizing that every blessing you have is from Allah, not from your own greatness.
*   **Opposite: Pride (*Kibr* / كِبْر):**
    *   The Prophet (pbuh) defined pride as: *"Rejecting the truth (*Batar al-Haqq*) and looking down on people (*Ghamt al-Nas*)."*
*   **The Spiritual Reality:**
    *   Allah says in the Quran: *"And walk not on the earth with pride. Verily, you cannot rend the earth asunder, nor reach the mountains in height."* (Surah al-Isra: 37).
*   **Prophetic Model:**
    *   The Prophet (pbuh) would repair his own shoes, milk his goats, and serve his family.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Ash'ari Spiritual Insight:** In Ash'ari spirituality (often taught through the works of classical theologians like Imam al-Ghazali), pride is a fatal sickness of the heart because it assumes that we are independent creators of our success. 
*   **Theology Check:** Remind students: since Allah is the sole Creator of all our talents, wealth, and beauty, boasting about them is intellectually false. We are merely *receivers* of Allah's gifts.
*   **Discussion Starter:** Ask: *"How does humility make a community stronger? How does pride destroy friendships?"*

---

## Slide 6: Controlling Anger: The Power of Hilm
### Forbearance (Hilm) vs. Explosive Rage (Ghadab)
*   **What is Ghadab?**
    *   **Ghadab** (غَضَب) is anger. It is a spark from Shaytan that clouds human intellect (*'Aql*).
*   **The Key Virtues:**
    *   **Kadhm al-Ghaydh** (كَظْم الْغَيْظ): Suppressing rage when you have the power to act on it.
    *   **Hilm** (حِلْم): Forbearance and emotional control, developing a calm, gentle nature over time.
*   **The Prophetic Standard:**
    *   *"The strong person is not the one who can wrestle others down; the strong person is the one who controls himself in moments of anger."* (Muwatta Malik).
*   **Practical Steps to Control Anger:**
    1.  Seek refuge in Allah: Say *A'udhu billahi min ash-Shaytan ir-Rajeem*.
    2.  Change posture: If standing, sit down; if sitting, lie down.
    3.  Perform Wudu: Cool the physical heat of anger with water.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Textual Focus:** Highlight that Imam Malik placed the Hadith about controlling anger prominently in the *Muwatta*.
*   **Anatomy of Anger:** Explain that anger starts in the heart but manifests in the body. The Sunnah teaches physical hacks (changing posture, Wudu) to disrupt the biological cycle of rage.
*   **Activity:** Have students role-play a scenario where someone insults them. Practice pausing, taking a breath, and responding with *Hilm*.

---

## Slide 7: Creed Connection: Anger, Patience, and Divine Decree
### Connecting Character to Qadar
*   **The Ash'ari View on Qadar (Divine Decree):**
    *   Everything that happens in the universe (both what we like and what we dislike) occurs by Allah's Will (*Iradah*), Knowledge (*'Ilm*), and Power (*Qudrah*).
*   **Anger as Resistance to Decree:**
    *   When we react with explosive anger to accidents, delays, or difficulties, we are, in a spiritual sense, reacting against what Allah has decreed.
*   **Patience (*Sabr*) and Contentment (*Rida*):**
    *   Recognizing that an annoying event (e.g., losing a game, dropping a plate) was decreed by Allah allows us to say: *Qaddara Allahu wa ma sha'a fa'ala* ("Allah has decreed, and what He wills, He does").
    *   This instantly diffuses anger and replaces it with spiritual peace.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Deepening Belief:** This is a crucial Ash'ari theological application. Connect the sixth pillar of Iman (belief in *Qadar*) directly to everyday emotional control.
*   **Clarification:** Emphasize that accepting *Qadar* does not mean we do not try to fix bad situations. If someone harms us, we seek justice. But we do not lose our inner peace or descend into rage, because we know Allah is in absolute control.
*   **Reflection:** *"How does knowing that an accident was already written in the Preserved Tablet (Al-Lawh al-Mahfudh) make it easier to forgive the person who caused it?"*

---

## Slide 8: Character and the Law: The Concept of Muru'ah
### Nobility and Legal Competency in Maliki Fiqh
*   **What is Muru'ah?**
    *   **Muru'ah** (مُرُوءَة) translates to chivalry, dignity, and honorable behavior.
    *   It means acting in a way that respects local customs, is polite, and avoids foolishness.
*   **The Maliki Legal Link:**
    *   To testify in an Islamic court of law, a witness must have **'Adalah** (عَدَالَة), upright legal character.
    *   In Maliki fiqh, a person's **'Adalah** is ruined if they lack **Muru'ah**!
*   **What destroys Muru'ah?**
    *   Public tantrums and screaming.
    *   Eating while walking in the street (traditionally considered undignified in classical societies).
    *   Playing foolish pranks, lying for clout, or dressing inappropriately in public.
*   **Ruling:** If you lack *Muru'ah*, your testimony is **rejected** by a Maliki judge (*Qadi*).

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Fiqh Literacy Focus:** This is a unique, powerful concept. Most students think good manners are optional. Show them that in Maliki law, bad character has direct legal consequences.
*   **Historical Context:** Explain that what violates *Muru'ah* can change slightly based on time and place (*'Urf*, custom), but the core principle remains: a Muslim must behave with dignity. 
*   **Discussion:** Ask: *"What are things people do today on social media (like prank videos) that would destroy their Muru'ah in the eyes of a Maliki judge?"*

---

## Slide 9: Rights of Parents (Birr al-Walidayn)
### The Divine Equation
*   **The Quranic Command:**
    *   Allah says: *"And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment."* (Surah al-Isra: 23).
    *   Allah pairs the duty of worshiping Him directly with the duty of honoring parents!
*   **Birr al-Walidayn** (بِرّ الْوَالِدَيْن):
    *   *Birr* is the highest form of active goodness, love, obedience, and respect.
*   **The Ultimate Limit: Say No "Uff":**
    *   Allah forbids even the smallest sigh of frustration (*"Uff"* / أُفّ) toward parents.
*   **What if they command disobedience to Allah?**
    *   We do not obey them in sin, but we must still maintain gentle, kind companionship with them in worldly matters.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Theological Link:** Point out the sequencing in the Quran. Worship of Allah is the primary right (*Haqq Allah*), and honoring parents is the primary human right (*Haqq al-Adami*).
*   **Obedience Rules:** Clarify that obedience to parents is obligatory (*Wajib*) in everything that is permissible (*Mubah*) or recommended (*Mandub*). It is forbidden to obey them if they command you to leave a clear obligation (like Salah) or commit a sin (like lying).
*   **Vocabulary:** *Birr* (righteousness/extreme goodness) and *Uff* (sound of annoyance).

---

## Slide 10: Legal Rights of Parents in Maliki Law
### Specific Fiqh Rulings
*   **1. Parental Permission for Voluntary Deeds:**
    *   In Maliki fiqh, a child **must** obtain parental permission before embarking on voluntary travel, voluntary military service, or long-term voluntary study away from home if the parents will suffer from their absence.
*   **2. Financial Maintenance (*Nafaqah* / نَفَقَة):**
    *   If parents become poor and cannot support themselves, it is a **strict legal obligation** on their children (who have means) to pay for their food, clothing, housing, and medical care.
*   **3. Testimonial Boundaries:**
    *   In the Maliki school, a child's testimony in court **in favor** of their parents is generally not accepted because of the natural bias of love. However, testifying *against* them is restricted to preserve parent-child honor.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Fiqh Literacy Details:** Detail the legal nature of *Birr*. It is not just about being polite; it has financial and legal components.
*   **Nafaqah:** Explain that under Islamic law, maintenance (*nafaqah*) is reciprocal. Parents must support young children, and adult children must support elderly, poor parents. This is enforceable by a court.
*   **Discussion:** Why do you think the Maliki school requires parental permission for voluntary travel? (Answer: Because serving parents and keeping their hearts at ease is a higher obligation (*Fard*) than voluntary travels).

---

## Slide 11: Keeping Family Ties (Silat al-Rahim)
### The Sacred Bonds of Kinship
*   **What is Rahim?**
    *   **Rahim** (رَحِم) literally means "womb." 
    *   **Silat al-Rahim** (صِلَة الرَّحِم) means connecting and maintaining relationships with blood relatives (grandparents, siblings, aunts, uncles, cousins).
*   **The Severity of Severing Ties (*Qat' al-Rahim*):**
    *   Severing family ties is a major sin (*Kabirah*).
    *   The Prophet (pbuh) said: *"The severer of family ties will not enter Paradise."* (Agreed upon).
*   **How to maintain ties?**
    *   Visiting them, calling them, sending gifts, helping them financially when they are in need, and forgiving them when they hurt us.
    *   The Prophet (pbuh) said: *"The one who maintains ties is not the one who merely reciprocates. Rather, it is the one who, when his ties are severed, connects them."* (Bukhari).

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Explanation:** Emphasize that *Silat al-Rahim* is not just about visiting relatives who are nice to us. The true test of this virtue is when a relative is distant or rude, and we still make the effort to contact them for the sake of Allah.
*   **Language Tip:** Explain that *Rahim* is derived from Allah's name *Al-Rahman* (The Merciful). The womb represents mercy and connection.
*   **Discussion:** *"How can we maintain family ties with relatives who live far away in other countries?"* (e.g., video calls, sending messages, visiting during holidays).

---

## Slide 12: Rights of Neighbors (Huquq al-Jiwar)
### The Sacred Radius of the Community
*   **The Prophetic Warning:**
    *   The Prophet (pbuh) said: *"Angel Jibril kept advising me to treat neighbors kindly until I thought he would make them my heirs."* (Agreed upon).
*   **Defining the Neighbor in Maliki Fiqh:**
    *   How far does the "neighborhood" go?
    *   **The Maliki Standard:** The neighborhood extends to **forty (40) houses** in every direction (front, back, left, and right).
*   **Core Duties to Neighbors:**
    1.  **Guarding their safety:** Never harming them with noise, smell, or actions.
    2.  **Generosity:** Sharing food, greeting them, and helping them in times of distress.
    3.  **Covering their faults:** Protecting their privacy and dignity.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **The 40-House Rule:** Explain the spatial imagination of Islamic law. It does not just mean the person next door; it means the entire local micro-community of 40 houses.
*   **Hadith Check:** Emphasize the strong language of the Prophet (pbuh): *"He is not a believer whose neighbor is not safe from his harm (*Bawa'iq*)."* (Muslim).
*   **Actionable Advice:** Encourage students to think of small acts of kindness: sharing food with a neighbor, shoveling snow from their walkway, or simply smiling and greeting them.

---

## Slide 13: Property & Neighborhood Rights in Maliki Law
### Specific Legal Safeguards
*   **1. Prevention of Harm (*Da'f al-Darar*):**
    *   In Maliki fiqh, a property owner is **legally blocked** from using their property in a way that causes direct harm to their neighbor.
    *   *Examples:* Building a high wall that blocks the neighbor's sunlight, opening a window that directly overlooks a neighbor's private courtyard, or venting smoke towards their house.
*   **2. Right of Pre-emption (*Shuf'ah* / شُفْعَة):**
    *   If you share property or a common access pathway with a neighbor, and you want to sell your share, you **must offer it to your partner/neighbor first** before selling it to a stranger. 
    *   This prevents unwanted or harmful strangers from encroaching on the neighborhood.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Fiqh Literacy Focus:** Introduce *Shuf'ah* (Pre-emption). This is a highly developed contract law concept in Maliki fiqh that directly serves social harmony (*Maslahah*).
*   **Darar (Harm):** The Maliki school is very strict on *Darar*. While other schools might say "It's my property, I can build what I want," the Malikis enforce the Prophetic rule: *"There shall be no harming nor reciprocating harm"* (*La darar wa la dirar*).
*   **Application:** If a neighbor complains to a Maliki judge that someone built a window specifically to spy on their family, the judge will order the window to be blocked.

---

## Slide 14: Choosing Companions: The Ethics of Friendship
### The Company You Keep Shapes Your Soul
*   **Suhbah Salihah** (صُحْبَة صَالِحَة): Good, righteous companionship.
*   **The Prophetic Analogy:**
    *   *The Good Friend:* Like a seller of perfume (*Misk*). Even if you do not buy perfume, you leave smelling good.
    *   *The Bad Friend:* Like a blacksmith working a bellows. He either burns your clothes with flying sparks or leaves you smelling like foul smoke.
*   **The Spiritual Influence:**
    *   The Prophet (pbuh) said: *"A person is on the religion of his close friend (*Khalil*), so let each of you look to whom he takes as a close friend."* (Abu Dawud).

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Analysis of the Perfume/Blacksmith Hadith:** Explain that influence is often silent and subconscious. You do not have to copy your friend's bad behavior immediately; just sitting with them regularly causes your heart to become desensitized to sin.
*   **Vocabulary:** *Khalil* (intimate, ultimate friend, a step higher than *Sadiq*).
*   **Discussion:** Ask: *"How do your friends influence the way you talk? The games you play? The way you speak to your parents?"*

---

## Slide 15: Friendship in Court: Maliki Rulings on Witness Testimony
### The Legal Reality of Friendship
*   **The Maliki View on Biased Testimony:**
    *   Islamic law requires witnesses to be completely objective.
    *   In the Maliki school, a person's testimony in court **in favor of their very close friend** (*Shahadat al-Sadiq li-Sadiqihi*) is **rejected**.
*   **Why?**
    *   The legal system recognizes that the bond of close friendship (*Sadaqah*) is so strong that a friend might lie, exaggerate, or overlook the truth out of loyalty to their friend.
*   **The Higher Standard:**
    *   True Islamic friendship does not mean lying for your friend in court. It means helping them stay on the path of truth, even if the truth is against them.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Fiqh Literacy Concept:** Show the students how the legal reality of friendship is codified in law. In the Maliki school, the judge will ask: *"What is the relationship between the witness and the claimant?"* If they are intimate friends who eat, travel, and share secrets, the testimony is disqualified due to *Tuhmah* (suspicion of bias).
*   **Moral Lesson:** Emphasize that loyalty to Allah and justice (*'Adl*) always comes before loyalty to a friend. 
*   **Hadith Connection:** *"Help your brother whether he is the oppressor or the oppressed."* The Companions asked how to help the oppressor. The Prophet (pbuh) replied: *"By stopping him from oppressing."* (Bukhari).

---

## Slide 16: Confronting Peer Pressure
### Standing Strong in the Face of Fitan (Trials)
*   **What is Peer Pressure?**
    *   The psychological and social force that pushes you to conform to the behavior of those around you to fit in.
*   **Islamic Goal: Guarding the Deen (*Hifdh al-Din*):**
    *   Our primary objective is to protect our faith and relationship with Allah.
*   **Strategies to Resist Peer Pressure:**
    1.  **Define your boundaries early:** If people know you pray and do not lie, they will not ask you to cheat.
    2.  **The power of "No":** Saying "No" is a sign of *Muru'ah* (strength of character) and *Izzah* (honorable pride in Islam).
    3.  **Seek alternative company:** If a group makes you feel bad for practicing your Deen, walk away.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Pedagogical Discussion:** Peer pressure is one of the biggest challenges for 10-13 year olds. Keep this practical.
*   **Vocabulary:** *Fitan* (plural of *Fitnah*, trials, temptations, confusion).
*   **Scenario Exercise:** Ask students: *"Your friends are laughing at a classmate behind their back and tell you to join in. If you don't, they'll call you a coward. What do you do?"* Discuss how to walk away or change the topic.

---

## Slide 17: Social Media & The Muslim Mindset
### Guarding the Five Necessities (Al-Daruriyyat al-Khams)
*   In Islamic law, the Shariah is designed to protect five essential things: **Religion (*Din*), Life (*Nafs*), Intellect (*'Aql*), Honor/Lineage (*'Ird* / *Nasl*), and Wealth (*Mal*)**.
*   **How does Social Media impact these?**
    *   **Guarding the Mind (*Hifdh al-'Aql*):** Social media algorithms feed addictive content that wastes time and distracts from deep thought.
    *   **Guarding Honor (*Hifdh al-'Ird* / حِفْظ الْعِرْض):** Social media makes it easy to gossip (*Ghibah*), spread rumors (*Namimah*), spy on others (*Tajassus*), and expose people's private faults.
*   **The Islamic Golden Rule online:**
    *   If you would not say it to someone's face in front of their parents, do not type it online.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Theological & Legal framework:** Introduce the *Daruriyyat al-Khams* (The Five Necessities) which are the core objectives of the Shariah (*Maqasid al-Shariah*).
*   **Application:** Show how modern technology challenges these ancient legal protections. 
    *   *Honor ('Ird):* Spreading a screenshot of a private chat to humiliate someone is a direct attack on their *'Ird*, which is a major sin in Islam.
    *   *Intellect ('Aql):* Mindless scrolling damages the mind's ability to focus on Salah and Quran.

---

## Slide 18: Blocking the Paths to Harm: Sadd al-Dhara'i'
### A Key Maliki Rule for the Digital Age
*   **What is Sadd al-Dhara'i'?**
    *   **Sadd al-Dhara'i'** (سَدّ الذَّرَائِع) is a famous Maliki legal principle meaning: **"Blocking the means to evil."**
    *   If a permissible action almost always leads to a forbidden result (*Haram*), the Maliki school rules that the action itself becomes restricted or prohibited.
*   **Applying the Principle Online:**
    *   *Example 1:* Following accounts that post inappropriate content. Even if you say "I won't copy them," the path leads to sin. Therefore, you must block or unfollow them (*Sadd al-Dhara'i'*).
    *   *Example 2:* Joining chat groups where cyberbullying or gossiping occurs. The path leads to participating in *Ghibah*. You must leave the group.
*   **Proactive Protection:** We guard our eyes, ears, and hearts before the sin even starts.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Fiqh Literacy Focus:** Explain the concept of *Sadd al-Dhara'i'* clearly. It is one of the defining features of Maliki jurisprudence. While some schools look only at the final act, Imam Malik looked at the pathways that lead to the act.
*   **Interactive Challenge:** Ask the class: *"What is an app or feature on your phone that you had to delete or turn off because it kept leading you to waste time or see bad things?"* Explain that this action of deleting it is a practical application of *Sadd al-Dhara'i'*.

---

## Slide 19: Justice ('Adl) and Equity (Qist)
### The Universal Scales of Islam
*   **What is 'Adl?**
    *   **'Adl** (عَدْل) means justice, putting everything in its proper place, and giving everyone their due right.
*   **What is Qist?**
    *   **Qist** (قِسْط) is equity, ensuring fairness in practical distribution and treatment, taking into account individual circumstances.
*   **The Command to be Just to All:**
    *   Allah says: *"O you who believe! Stand out firmly for justice, as witnesses to Allah, even though it be against yourselves, or your parents, or your kin..."* (Surah an-Nisa: 135).
*   **Opposite: Oppression (*Zulm* / ظُلْم):**
    *   Allah says in a Hadith Qudsi: *"O My servants! I have forbidden oppression (*Zulm*) for Myself, and I have made it forbidden among you, so do not oppress one another."* (Muslim).

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Vocabulary Differentiation:** Clarify the nuance between *'Adl* (strict justice/equality under the law) and *Qist* (distributive equity/fairness that accounts for differences). 
*   **Illustration:** If you have two siblings (one is 5 years old and the other is 15 years old), giving them both the exact same shoe size is "equal" but unjust. Giving them sizes that fit them is *Qist*.
*   **Crucial Creed Detail:** In Ash'ari theology, Allah is Al-'Adl. Because He is the absolute owner of creation, whatever He does is just by definition. Oppression (*Zulm*) is impossible for Allah because oppression means violating someone else's rights, and everything belongs to Allah.

---

## Slide 20: The Common Good: Maslahah Mursalah
### Using Maliki Legal Principles to Treat Others Well
*   **What is Maslahah Mursalah?**
    *   **Maslahah Mursalah** (مَصْلَحَة مُرْسَلَة) is a Maliki legal source meaning: **"Unrestricted Public Interest."**
    *   It refers to creating rules or taking actions that bring benefit or prevent harm to society, even if there is no specific Quranic text about that exact issue.
*   **Living the Principle:**
    *   How do we treat others well using *Maslahah*?
    *   *Example 1: Traffic Rules.* Stopping at red lights is not in the Quran, but it protects human life (*Maslahah*). We obey it as a religious duty.
    *   *Example 2: School Rules.* Keeping the classroom clean, not using phones during class, and recycling are actions that build a healthy environment for everyone.
*   **Being a force for good:** A Muslim is always looking for ways to benefit the community.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Fiqh Literacy Focus:** *Maslahah Mursalah* is another pillar of Maliki legal methodology (*Usul al-Fiqh*). Explain that Imam Malik was famous for using this principle to address new social problems.
*   **Connection to Character:** Show that a good Muslim does not just ask, *"Is there a specific rule forcing me to do this?"* Instead, they ask, *"Does this action help my community and please Allah?"*
*   **Discussion:** Ask: *"Can you think of a modern rule in your town or school that helps everyone, even though it was not around 1400 years ago?"* (e.g., speed limits, internet safety rules).

---

## Slide 21: Sources and Bibliography
### Building on Classical Foundations
*   **Primary Fiqh Texts:**
    *   Imam Malik ibn Anas, *Al-Muwatta* (Collection of Hadith and legal practice of Madinah).
    *   Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani, *Al-Risalah* (The classical Maliki manual of law).
    *   Al-Hattab al-Maliki, *Mawahib al-Jalil* (Comprehensive commentary on Maliki fiqh).
*   **Primary Creed & Akhlaq Texts:**
    *   Imam al-Sanusi, *Al-Aqidah al-Sanusiyyah* (Standard Ash'ari creed).
    *   Imam al-Ghazali, *Ihya 'Ulum al-Din* (Revival of the Religious Sciences - Akhlaq section).
    *   Imam al-Qarafi, *Al-Furuq* (Maliki legal distinctions and public interest philosophy).
*   **Modern Fiqh Literacy Reference:**
    *   Commentaries on the *Risalah* of Al-Qayrawani.

---
**Teacher Notes:**
*   **Closing Remarks:** Encourage students to appreciate that the rules of character, social media, and family rights are not arbitrary. They are built on the deep, intellectual inheritance of the Maliki and Ash'ari schools.
*   **Review:** Do a quick verbal quiz on the terms learned: *Sidq*, *Tawadu'*, *Muru'ah*, *Shuf'ah*, *Sadd al-Dhara'i'*, *Maslahah Mursalah*.
